title: Resonant 14 — Stanley Tinn source-first mechanical study
status: Educational, favourable reduced model; not a recovered buildable design or validated flight prediction

photographs_read.reading: Mute swan planform, broad inner wing and rounded outer wing. Rounded Say column gives full span 7.4 ft and wrist span 3.7 ft = 50% b. Original paragraph gives total area 6.61 square feet and AR about 8.29, with uncertainty from specimens and spreading.
photographs_read.used: aspect_ratio = 7.4*7.4/6.61 = 8.284417549167927; wrist_span_fraction = 3.7/7.4 = 0.5; full-scale area = 196/aspect_ratio. Broad constant inner chord and tapered four-segment elliptical outer planform.
photographs_read.uncertain_or_excluded: The inconsistent 3.135 ft wing-length conversion is excluded. Handwritten changes near the area paragraph are not treated as measured replacements. The later 7.83 comparison is not substituted for the requested original-area calculation.
photographs_read.completion: 14 m full span, 0.25 m hinge offsets and normalised full-scale chord are engineering assumptions.

photographs_read.reading: Göttingen 417a curved-plate section chart with several axes and curves labelled with low Reynolds numbers, including 168,000 and 42,000.
photographs_read.used: Treat section aerodynamics as section-specific and distinguish lift, drag and moment context.
photographs_read.uncertain_or_excluded: Axis associations and exact curve values are ambiguous; no exact coefficient digitisation or full-scale extrapolation is claimed.
photographs_read.completion: Separate supplied illustrative inner/outer CL and CD arrays, endpoint-clamped linear interpolation, distinct camber gains and nominal-AR induced drag.

photographs_read.reading: Bird flight as a guide to ornithopter design, copyright 2007 Stanley J. O. Tinn. Proposes a sine-wave ideal trajectory and deriving the range of required vertical force, then evaluating candidate wing actions using steady aerodynamics; explicitly discusses manned mechanical flight.
photographs_read.used: Human-piloted machine; actual wing forces are compared against a target rather than prescribing the aircraft trajectory.
photographs_read.uncertain_or_excluded: Historical annotations and missing referenced appendices do not supply a numerical aircraft specification.
photographs_read.completion: Supplied seated 55 kg adult, 6 m fuselage, engine-powered 14 m aircraft and independent free COM dynamics.

photographs_read.reading: Straight and level flapping flight cannot be exactly straight and level: cyclic lift and thrust cause an undulating trajectory and unsteady airspeed. Discusses bounding and ring-gait wakes; continued work towards a powered man-carrying ornithopter.
photographs_read.used: Instantaneous local forces, rather than constant thrust or smoothed lift; permit small wingbeat motion.
photographs_read.uncertain_or_excluded: No numerical wake law or validated human-carrying performance is provided; marginal handwritten sentence is not used quantitatively.
photographs_read.completion: Quasi-steady strip model omits ring vortices and wake history.

photographs_read.reading: At low speed the downstroke lasts longer than recovery; at cruising speed periods become equal. Wing-wishbone-body assembly can be modelled as resonant. Compare lift and drag from candidate wing action with forces needed for the desired trajectory.
photographs_read.used: Fixed low-speed timing bias 0.3 or cruise bias 0, sinusoidal phase-warped linkage, elastic exchange and diagnostic target-force panel.
photographs_read.uncertain_or_excluded: Heavy marginal revisions to the trajectory/acceleration paragraph are uncertain; no marginal equation is silently recovered.
photographs_read.completion: Exact phase curves, 28,000 Nm/rad spring, inertia and damping coefficients are supplied engineering completions, not notebook samples.

photographs_read.reading: Wing/body inertias and wishbone spring act about common CG. Fore/aft wing motion changes lift/CG separation, giving pitching moment with tail assistance. Wing action has inner arm and outer hand; hand moves down/back on working stroke and closes while trailing on recovery.
photographs_read.used: Distributed constant wing mass, moving whole-aircraft CG, coupled phase/pitch mass matrix, real fore/aft sweep work and reaction, two articulations and outer recovery overlap.
photographs_read.uncertain_or_excluded: No reliable numerical linkage dimensions, nonlinear spring law or exact resonance frequency is supplied.
photographs_read.completion: Two rigid sliding half-length leaves, 0.8 m sweep amplitude and finite-difference geometry derivatives are engineering assumptions. No animal feathers or free spring energy.

photographs_read.reading: Opening continuation explicitly says reduced area and span on recovery, then adjustment of local incidences; handwritten addition mentions camber. Later goshawk example shows section profiles and camber 13%, 10%, 9%, 6%.
photographs_read.used: Independent camber, twist/incidence and exposure channels; curved production geometry and section lift change with camber.
photographs_read.uncertain_or_excluded: Goshawk dimensions and percentages are not mute-swan specifications and are not copied into this machine.
photographs_read.completion: Supplied inner camber 0.022 +/- 0.008 and outer 0.045 +/- 0.015, with separate section thickness metadata.

photographs_read.reading: Inner arm thickness 5–6%; outer hand effectively thin slotted curved plate. Local lift/drag can largely act as forward thrust and vertical lift at low speed. Trailing and partial closing reduce recovery area and drag. Conventional tail/weight-shift suitable for an elementary ornithopter, fin/rudder advantageous with longer moment arm. Takeoff example quotes inner -15 to +45 degrees and hand +/-45 degrees.
photographs_read.used: Inner structural section, thin overlapping curved leaves, local force vector resolution, conventional tail and rudder, readable gearing and three-wheel runway gear.
photographs_read.uncertain_or_excluded: Biological takeoff angles and suggested stiffness changes are qualitative context, not the full-scale machine's required cam settings. Water-ski landing is not implemented.
photographs_read.completion: Thickness ratios 0.055/0.008; supplied amplitudes, finite controls, tail incidence and passive pitch damping; wheeled rather than water takeoff.

photographs_read.reading: Glide drag W/(L/D), power D*V (550 imperial conversion). Additional terms include induced drag, horizontal acceleration/deceleration, cyclic height and wing inertia. Inertial power is zero for zero damping. Refers to a missing design algorithm in Appendix 12.
photographs_read.used: Actual aerodynamic dissipation and coupled mechanical energy; conservative spring cannot propel aircraft without motor work. Separate frozen unpowered glide configuration.
photographs_read.uncertain_or_excluded: Missing appendices, tentative 25% inertial-efficiency suggestion and handwritten dimensional note are not treated as validated aircraft coefficients.
photographs_read.completion: Finite 16 kW shaft cap, 85% transmission, fuel BSFC, work integration and supplied derived glide trim. Approach follows the current task: already powered at 16 m/s and omega 6, not a free-energy restart.

engineering_assumptions.mass: 173.9 kg dry including 55 kg seated adult; 3.6 kg fuel; 177.5 kg initially. Supplied component allocations retained, including all 30 kg of wings even during overlap.
engineering_assumptions.powertrain: 16.9 kg engine-package reference is supplied, not Stanley's selection. Finite nonnegative starting torque, capped shaft power, governor error torque, reflected drive inertia and transmission efficiency are illustrative assumptions.
engineering_assumptions.dynamics: Actual geometric two-coordinate mass matrix and derivatives, COM translation, midpoint RK2 at substeps no greater than 1/240 s. Ground uses three-wheel pitch-zero constraint and moving-CG phase inertia with nonnegative normal-load release.
engineering_assumptions.stability: Supplied 1000 Nm s/rad passive pitch damping is used as a dissipative torque, not an autopilot. No pitch target or flight-path hold; neutral bank holds bank after its finite roll rate damps.
engineering_assumptions.rendering: Engineered teal tubular frame, cream curved fabric, brass linkage hardware, exposed engine and belt reduction, spring cartridges, seated restrained adult, conventional empennage and three lateral-axle tyres. Decorative rib caps follow identical material coordinates; host owns actual panel geometry.
engineering_assumptions.timing: Low-speed timing bias is fixed for a run. Motor-off coasts; no automatic glide change, timing change or prescribed wing speed.

limitations: No structural, fatigue, aeroelastic, propulsive-efficiency or human-flight safety validation.
Section coefficients are favourable full-scale illustrative assumptions, not measured from photo 08.
No unsteady wakes, stall hysteresis, overlap-flow interaction, flexible leaves or section pitching moments.
Roll/yaw inertial coupling is omitted; banking rotates the actual force without vertical lift compensation.
Ground is a reduced rigid three-wheel constraint, not suspension or detailed tyre deformation.
Visual engine detail, frame diameters, materials and control routing are design interpretations, not recovered construction drawings.
No execution, tests, builds, browser preview or grader feedback were requested; only source reading and mental review were available.
